newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai to spend 3 pct of GDP on environment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai to spend 3 pct of GDP on environment.

text.p: Shanghai will invest three per cent of its gross domestic product (GDP) on environmmental protection over the next four years, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.

The newspaper said the city's environmental efforts would focus on the protection of the headwaters of the Huangpu River and the clean-up of Suzhou Creek, the two main waterways running through the city.
Between eight and nine billion yuan will be invested in environmental protection each year of the current Ninth Five-year Plan, lasting from 1996 to 2000, it said.
It said city officials hoped "Suzhou Creek, now black and putrid with pollution, will be clean by the year 2000".
Other measures planned include the phase-out of gasoline-powered mopeds in favour of electric ones and the use of lead-free gasoline.
The newspaper said regulations would be enacted to force 40 percent of Shanghai's vehicles to use lead-free fuel by the year 2000.

Shanghai, China's largest industrial city, has major problems with air and water pollution, but is given high marks by foreign environmental experts for the efforts it is making to clean things up even as the city's economy expands at an annual rate of more than 10 percent.
